why: The paper releases no code (no repository, no code_links, no stated compute), so there is nothing to run as-is. The target claim C1 is a single L2-regularised logistic regression on a public 7,043-row tabular dataset with a standard sklearn pipeline (label/one-hot encoding, min-max scaling, SMOTE on the training partition only, stratified 80/20 split, fixed 0.5 threshold). That is cheap and fully specified in the claim contract and Table 1 config, so the cheapest faithful path is to reimplement the pipeline from the paper text and the claim contract rather than hunt for author artefacts.
missing_artifacts: author code for preprocessing / model training / evaluation (never released)
exact random seed(s) and sklearn/imbalanced-learn/XGBoost/LightGBM versions used for Table 1
hyperparameters for XGBoost and LightGBM (C2) — not specified in the paper
IBM Telco Customer Churn CSV (public, but must be fetched manually from Kaggle 'blastchar/telco-customer-churn'; Kaggle API credentials may be needed)
SHAP/LIME analysis scripts and the CRM four-layer workflow artefacts (not needed for the match target C1)
blockers_seen: no author repository or code link anywhere in the contract
Kaggle download requires an authenticated API token or a manual CSV drop; a mirror/alternative URL must be used if credentials are unavailable
Python 3.12 is fine for modern sklearn/imbalanced-learn, but historical library versions from the paper are not pinned, so exact bit-level reproduction of 0.8411 is not guaranteed
single 80/20 split means the reported AUC depends on the seed; only the 5-fold CV claim (C4, 0.845±0.013) is seed-robust

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: about 6-10 minutes of command time: ~3 minutes to install scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn and pandas, ~1 minute to fetch the CSV, under 5 seconds to fit the logistic regression, and a few minutes for the 5-fold CV and the optional RF/XGB/LGBM comparison rows

compute.basis: 7,043 x 21 tabular CSV; a 40-feature logistic regression fit takes well under a second on CPU, SMOTE on 5,634 training rows is near-instant, and the full 5-fold CV plus the tree-model comparison rows is a few minutes of command time on an 8-core laptop.
